title: Adaptive JSON Mode Hysteresis and Saturation Backoff Tests
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Design and execute a suite of tests that validate JSON mode enforcement and constrained-decoding behavior under high-concurrency streaming workloads that include interleaved tool/function calls. This ticket focuses on hysteresis-based relaxation and saturation backoff: how the system gracefully relaxes schema strictness during brief capacity pressure and how it re-tightens constraints once stable. Tests will exercise per-tenant grace windows, primed KV-cache effects, and policy-driven fallback (shortened schema, placeholder fields, or model-variant hedging).
acceptance_criteria: Test harness can inject controlled load with streaming partial-emits and synthetic toolcall noise
Hysteresis thresholds configurable per-policy and observable in telemetry
Backoff behavior reduces downstream token costs while maintaining schema integrity for high-priority tenants
Canary run demonstrates no regression in P95 latency for non-degraded traffic and provides clear rollback signal
tasks: Implement test harness extension to simulate 0-1000 rps streaming clients with variable seq-length distributions
Add synthetic toolcall injector that returns noisy/late tool responses to simulate interference
Create policy matrix: strict | relaxed | hysteresis-window (ms) | saturation-threshold (conns) | fallback-variant
Instrument telemetry: hysteresis state transitions, per-tenant backoff counts, schema-violation events, and KV-cache hit correlation
Author canary plan and dashboard widgets for runtime-1.28
testing_plan: Baseline: 50 rps, mix of short chat and long-generation prompts, JSON mode strict. Verify schema pass rate >= 99.5%
Load ramp: gradually increase to saturation-threshold. Observe hysteresis window behaviour and record schema pass rate and token costs
Noise injection: interleave tool/function calls that return delayed or malformed responses and validate fallback policies are triggered appropriately
Per-tenant priority: run parallel tenants with high/low priority policies and confirm high-priority tenants preserve stricter constraints under identical load
KV-cache priming: pre-warm cache for a subset of requests and measure reduction in backoff triggers compared to cold cache runs

notes: Goal is resilience-first: occasional schema relaxation allowed for low-priority tenants to reduce costly fallbacks, but strict invariants for regulated customers must be enforced without compromise.
We will correlate schema-violation events with downstream user-visible errors to validate customer impact assumptions.
Consider follow-up ticket for automated rollout: adjust hysteresis thresholds based on observed sustained error rates and latencies.
